claim: Romerijo on Ribera del Marisco is a 70-year-old institution with separate cocedero (boiled) and freiduría (fried) counters where you pick seafood served in paper cones (papelón/cucurucho) to eat at tables or take away.
quote: Romerijo has played a pivotal role in the commercial development of La Ribera del Marisco, the city's most popular gastronomic district. Guests select the fresh products they wish to enjoy at the cooking station, which are then served in their signature paper cones.

claim: At Romerijo order gamba blanca gorda, langostino de Sanlúcar, cañaíllas and quisquillas at the counter; nearby La Venancia (Plaza de las Galeras Reales) is a classic Andalusian tavern for varied pescaíto frito (acedías, boquerones, puntillitas) and pastel de corvina.
quote: Romerijo — Specialties: Gamba blanca gorda, langostino de Sanlúcar, cañaíllas, quisquillas... La Venancia — Must-try: Pastel de corvina, varied pescaíto frito (acedías, boquerones, puntillitas). Classic Andalusian tavern.

claim: El Puerto's seafood spread covers bocas, nécoras, percebes, camarones, cañaíllas, cigalas and langostinos; pescaíto frito perfumes the streets, and a signature local dish is caldillo de perro made with fresh hake; the tapas route runs along Calle Misericordia, Ribera del Marisco and the promenade.
quote: pescaíto frito que impregnan de un olor característico las calles del municipio. A signature dish is caldillo de perro, made with fresh large hake... tapas route through bars on Calle Misericordia, the Ribera del Marisco waterfront area, and the maritime promenade.

claim: Atún rojo de almadraba is an El Puerto specialty best from April to June; Tritón Gastrobar (C. Ribera del Marisco 6) serves red-tuna tataki, marinated tacos and tartare with avocado and seaweed chips.
quote: red tuna from almadraba (a traditional fishing method). The optimal season... is April-June... Tritón Gastrobar... Red tuna tataki with soy sauce and ginger; Red tuna marinaded tacos; Red tuna tartare with avocado and seaweed chips.

claim: Bodegas Obregón is an authentic central El Puerto tabanco serving sherry (Fino, Amontillado, Oloroso) poured straight from the barrel with weekend hot tapas like chicken cooked in Pedro Ximénez (~€5.50); cash-only, crowded, locals-heavy.
quote: serves sherry and other wines directly from wooden barrels... On weekends, they offer hot tapas and traditional Cadiz dishes. One reviewer noted it serves chicken cooked in Pedro Ximenez (sweet sherry) for around €5.50... bring cash.

claim: Toro Tapas, set within the Bodegas Osborne wine-tourism complex, is a top-rated El Puerto tapas spot (user rating 9.3) for dishes like tortillitas de camarones and pescaíto frito (~€25-35 pp).
quote: Toro Tapas with a rating of 9.3... a renowned restaurant located within the Bodegas Osborne Wine Tourism complex... high-quality and challenging cuisine.
